utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-03-66-PT, the Prosecutor versus Limaj, Bala, and Musliu. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: I'm sorry, but this doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the interpreters now? JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Yes. Okay. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour, good afternoon, my name is Andrew Cayley. I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor with my colleague Mr. Alex Whiting. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: And there for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it please, Your Honour, Karim Khan for Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tome Gashi for Haradin Bala.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Peter Murphy also for Haradin Bala, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bajram Krasniqi for Isak Musliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour, Steven Powles for Isak Musliu. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Thank you. This is the first time I am appearing with these parties in this process, I will present myself also. My name is Joaquin Martin Canivell. I am the last arrived Ad Litem Judge, and as you well know, the statute for the Tribunal has been recently changed so as to allow Ad Litem Judges to participate in this pre-trial work. So that is the reason for my being here today. I had read about the meeting you have had yesterday, and I would like to mention a few points which I suppose would be of interest to the parties. First of all, we had already received an application, a motion for previous release of one of the accused, Mr. Limaj. We had to gather the necessary statements. I am confident that it will be soon made, and as soon as we get that, we will make -- prepare the request that has been made. I know that also one of the other accused, Mr. Bala, has also made or is planning to make a new application also for being released, and so I will consider it in due time and you will know when we have been informed about the problem and the situation of the health of this accused. By the way, I have to ask all of you, the accused, to stand up. Mr. Bala, please. I have to ask you if you understand the proceedings in a language that is comprehensible for you, is understandable for you. THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Thank you. You may sit down. Mr. Limaj, please. I have the same question for you. You understand the proceedings in a language that is comprehensible for you? THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Okay. Thank you. And then Mr. Musliu. Do you understand the proceedings in a language that is understandable for you? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Thank you. So we will continue. I suppose one very important point is related to the moment of disclosure of the information above all by the Prosecution to the counsel, the parties. I heard that -- well, you had arrived at an agreement yesterday. I hope that would be a possibility, if you keep the terms of this agreement, for allowing an expeditious disposal of this case. I think I am happy knowing that. I would also ask you -- tell you to remember that it is a possibility of arriving to an agreement of facts. Of course, in the time this Tribunal has already been working, many of the facts which are common from one case to the other had been -- sometimes has been rejected by the accused, but in the course of the proceedings some of the facts have been really so well proven that I would say it would be of little use, no use at all, to come again on that, that you can make an effort so as to reach agreements of these facts. That would be helpful also in the disposal of the case. On the other side, I had heard that the Prosecution has mentioned the possibility of speeding up, if possible, the case, the proceedings, and that perhaps will be able to start with the case in mid-February. So I also rejoice of this possibility and encourage you to keep going in this way so as to try to keep this alleged promised schedule. I had heard also about the difficulties you are having about the protection of some of the witnesses that you intend to call in the trial. I had realised that it could be complicated and difficult for you, but be sure that this Chamber is going to be very aware and very alert about how to take care of that and to try to help as much as possible on this. I don't know if there is any other subject that you would like me to mention, but in case I haven't mentioned all the aspects that you are interested in, I would call on you if you have any other subjects or issues that you would like to mention. To begin with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have nothing to add at this point, Your Honour. I believe that there are some requests that the Defence wish to make today, but I have no comments. I may have some comments if the Defence wish to raise any matters which I'm not aware of. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: So we'll start by the Defence. Please stand up and tell me what are the issues you would like to submit to this Trial Judge. Mr. Khan, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: If it please, Your Honour, a point of clarification at first instance. Following yesterday's conference, I fully accept, and indeed it's in the interest of all parties, to agree as many facts as are possible to ensure the expeditious conduct of the trial and to confine the issues, but it is also relevant to bear in mind that the previous jurisprudence of the Tribunal is of limited relevance to the factual allegations in this indictment, because this is the first KLA case, this is the first Kosovar case that is being prosecuted by the Prosecutor excluding the Milosevic case. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: But with that caveat, of course, we will try to come to whatever agreements we can. The aspect was alluded to in Your Honour's opening remarks. I would impress upon Your Honour to give early scrutiny to the application for provisional release in particular, in particular to the request that has been made that the Special Representative of the Secretary-General, His Excellency Michael Steiner, be contacted and be requested by the Trial Chamber to provide a statement in the terms that are detailed in the application. And the reasons for the -- the reasons in support of that are detailed in the application as well. But given the timetable and the departure anticipated departure of Mr. Steiner in August of 2003, I would urge you to give very early consideration of that matter. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Yes, of course. I am already aware of the problem with Mr. Steiner, and I'm really caring about that. Thank you for your application. Well, I don't know which of the counsel, so perhaps Mr. Bala would like to stand up and speak about if you have any special problem, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no particular problem. I only wish --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is experiencing a technical difficulty. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: We haven't got the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly urge you to contact Mr. Steiner as soon as possible. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Of course. I had told before that I would try to get in touch with Mr. Steiner as soon as possible. Okay. Anything else you would like to mention now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GASHI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not for the moment. Thank you, Your Honour. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Okay. Does any other of the counsel want to speak?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also support my -- the -- my colleague's application for the provisional release of Mr. Limaj and we have an intention to make an application for Mr. Musliu, and to be -- we will be open to mutual cooperation between the Prosecutor's office and the Defence side. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: There is no other question that you would like to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may raise one matter arising out of the Rule 65 ter meeting with the Prosecution yesterday. One matter that was dealt with yesterday was exculpatory material to be disclosed by the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 68. Your Honour may be aware that in the original indictment against the accused there was also a fourth accused, Mr. Agim Murtezi, who was arrested and transferred to The Hague initially with Mr. Musliu and Mr. Bala. He has subsequently been released and removed from the amended indictment. At this stage, the Defence are not aware of the circumstances that firstly led to his arrest and then the subsequent developments thereafter. Accordingly, the Defence would ask if the Prosecution could give an explanation of the process leading to his arrest and an eventual release, because this -- as this could clearly amount to exculpatory material. Accordingly, the Prosecution is formally asked to give a full explanation of those matters including all materials that may shed light on the process leading, firstly, to Mr. Murtezi's indictment and subsequent arrest and thereafter release and removal from the indictment. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: You think it could be helpful now at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Perhaps an initial explanation from the Prosecution could be of some assistance, but clearly there may be materials that the Prosecution may be obliged pursuant to Rule 68 to disclose in due course. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: What is the feeling of Mr. Cayley, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the obligation of the Prosecutor under Rule 68 is very clear, and it is to disclose to the Defence the existence of material known to the Prosecutor which in any way tends to suggest the innocence or mitigate the guilt of the accused or may affect the credibility of Prosecution evidence. That obligation covers all information, evidence, in our position in respect to the three accused that are there the courtroom at the moment. So the Rule 68 obligation in respect of the material that Mr. Powles is referring to, we will look at it and we will see if there is any Rule 68 material that is relevant to these three accused and we will disclose that material to counsel for the accused. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: So I think you mentioned it also yesterday in the meeting you had so you accept the obligation, of course, of what is said in Rule 68. Do you have any other explanation about the point you had? Rephrase it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: No. Thank you very much, Your Honour. I don't know if any of the other accused have any points to raise on this matter. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: So you may be assured. Okay. If nobody else wants to raise any other question -- would you like --

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. There is one other matter in connection with the motion that will be made for provisional release for Mr. Bala. Your Honour, one of the grounds of that would be Mr. Bala's medical condition. I will not go into the details of that in open session. However, we will also be making a motion for the preparation of a medical report that will have relevance to the motion for provisional release. I understand my learned friend Mr. Cayley has no objection to that motion. I would ask the Court, perhaps, to give an indication to the Registry that in view of the importance of moving the matter along that this report could be prepared as a matter of some urgency, and we do hope to file this motion by the end of this week. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Well, I understand that, and I call the attention of the Registrar to take care about that, and you can be sure that we will be as expedient as we can on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: I would like to ask now to the three accused persons, starting with Mr. Bala, please. Would you like to have any -- mention some problem about your status as a detained person now and something that doesn't work according to you and you would like to be bettered, ameliorated? Please speak up. THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would not say anything out of the ordinary regarding my detention. Everything is in order. We have all been treated in the same way. The most important thing that has not been done properly will be seen in the medical report. The question of my state of health which is not in order, this is a -- JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: You mean that -- [Albanian interpretation on English channel] THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] No. No. Everything is in order. I would say that the -- I have no, you see, atmosphere in the cell. I do not feel to be -- it's not a problem of the detention unit. It's about the place where I am in detention. And of course, political and economic and other problems. That's what I'm thinking of. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: You had mentioned at all these problems to the person ruling the Detention Unit so as to get relief that is possible to give you? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] It's true that I have nothing to comment on here. I'm treated the same as any other detainee. I have nothing to complain about, because conditions in the cell are the same for me as for the others. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: I understand. But you have medical assistance? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] Yes. I always get my medicines. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: And you had mentioned that to the doctor so that he can convey whatever is the problem to the administration of the Detention Unit? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] I have only seen the nurse who is there, and I don't know how far she's monitored the situation. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Okay. We will try to see about that. Any other question you would like to mention about your health. And your possibilities to communicate with your lawyer are all right? You have any problems? THE ACCUSED BALA: [Interpretation] So far I haven't had any opportunity to contact through the Registrar, but so far I haven't had any problems -- I have had possibilities. So far I have -- I haven't been able to communicate through the telephone of the secretariat, but through the lawyer I have been able to communicate now. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: You have these facilities, these possibilities to speak with and communicate with your counsel, and you can mention the problems you have so he can attract the attention of the Registry if necessary. Okay. You may sit down, please. Mr. Limaj, please. What is the situation that you feel -- THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] Thank you. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: -- with your stay in the Detention Unit? You have any problem about being taken care of and your health is taken care of properly? THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] First, thank you very much for the question and for asking me. So far I am well in health, and as for my stay, everything is in order and I am satisfied with the conditions and the way we are treated, and I have nothing else to raise today. Anything that I have to raise I will, of course, raise through my lawyer. And all my concerns, my ongoing concerns, I will convey through my lawyers, but so far everything is in order. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Okay. I wanted you to explain to -- speak to me that you know you can on this occasion make this application and to contact with me, yes, just to solve the problems you may have. You don't have any problems, I suppose, in relating with -- in contacting with your counsel? THE ACCUSED LIMAJ: [Interpretation] Thank you. So far, I have no -- nothing to raise, and no doubt I will make use of the -- make use of this opportunity, but so far everything is in order. Everything that I wish to raise, I will raise through my lawyer. But I would like to thank you for the excellent care that is being accorded to me by the leadership, and they have given me every opportunity to contact the people I need. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: You may sit down, please. And I ask also to Mr. Musliu. Do you have any issue you would like to raise or any problem you would like to mention about your situation in the Detention Unit and the care that is taken of you, if it is appropriate and you feel well taken care of. THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] I have no special question to issue. My physical state is good, everything is in order, and I don't have any kind of problem. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Now, have you any problem in communicating with your counsels? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] First of all, they are -- the telephone, we have not been accorded a privileged telephone to communicate with the other part -- with the lawyer, even though we communicate through the Registrar but require a privileged telephone. No doubt this will soon be done. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: But in any case, you want to communicate with your counsel. Your petition is accepted and taking care of, being solved appropriately? THE ACCUSED MUSLIU: [Interpretation] Yes. Every request is being considered. JUDGE MARTIN CANIVELL: Well, sit down, please. I suppose if there is nothing else of interest that could be raised here, we can end this meeting, not before I thank you for your help, the Registry and the counsels and Prosecutor and the interpreters also. So the meeting is concluded.

procedural_notes.text: ---  Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
